terms.definition: A collection of data about one topic, usually stored as a table with rows and columns.
terms.example: The Nkwen Traders dataset holds every sale from all four branches, from January to June 2026.

terms.definition: One line across a table. In a sales table, each row is usually one sale.
terms.example: One row shows a single sale: Mile 4 branch, Rice 50kg, 35,000 FCFA, paid with Mobile Money.

terms.definition: One line down a table. Each column holds one kind of information, such as date or price, for every row.
terms.example: The Branch column tells you where each sale happened: Nkwen, Mile 4, Commercial Avenue or Bafoussam Centre.

terms.definition: Data arranged in rows and columns, like a page of boxes in an exercise book.
terms.example: A products table lists each item's name, category and unit price in FCFA.

terms.definition: In Python, a name that stores a value. In statistics, a column whose value changes from row to row.
terms.example: price = 35000 stores the price of Rice 50kg; Quantity is a variable in the sales data.

terms.definition: Comma-separated values: a simple text file where each line is a row and commas separate the columns.
terms.example: nkwen_traders_sales.csv opens in Google Sheets or pandas; each line is one sale.

terms.definition: Data exactly as it was collected, before anyone has checked, fixed or cleaned it.
terms.example: In the raw data from the till, 'nkwen ', 'NKWEN' and 'Nkwen' appear as three different branches.

terms.definition: Finding and fixing problems in data, such as wrong spellings, missing values and duplicates, before you analyse it.
terms.example: Data cleaning turned 'Rice 50Kg' and 'rice 50kg' into one product name: 'Rice 50kg'.

terms.definition: An empty place in the data where a value should be. pandas shows it as NaN.
terms.example: Some Mile 4 sales have a missing value in PaymentMethod, so we do not know how the customer paid.

terms.definition: The kind of value something is: a whole number, a decimal number, text, True/False or a date.
terms.example: TotalSale_FCFA needs a number data type; stored as text, the sales cannot be added up.

terms.definition: A row or value that appears more than once when it should appear only once.
terms.example: The till sent one Mile 4 sale twice. The duplicate makes June revenue look higher than it really was.

terms.definition: Getting messy data into a useful shape: cleaning it, combining tables, changing its layout and adding columns.
terms.example: Data wrangling joined the Nkwen Traders sales and branches files and fixed their date formats.

terms.definition: When data or a method is unfair to some group, or pushes results away from the truth in one direction.
terms.example: Asking only Nkwen branch customers about prices gives bias: Bafoussam Centre customers are not heard.

terms.definition: Any information that can identify a real person, such as a name, phone number or Mobile Money number.
terms.example: Customers' phone numbers are personal data, so Nkwen Traders must protect them under Cameroon's 2024 law.

terms.definition: Showing data as a picture, such as a chart or map, so people can see patterns quickly.
terms.example: A bar chart of sales by branch is a simple data visualization for Nkwen Traders managers.

terms.definition: One screen of charts and key numbers, often updated automatically, that gives a quick view of performance.
terms.example: The Nkwen Traders dashboard shows total revenue, number of transactions and sales for each branch.

terms.definition: Structured Query Language: a language for asking questions of data stored in a database.
terms.example: With SQL, you can get total sales for each Nkwen Traders branch in three short lines.

terms.definition: A file made of rows and columns of cells, such as Google Sheets or Excel, where you type data and formulas.
terms.example: The Mile 4 manager records daily stock of Rice 50kg in a spreadsheet.

terms.definition: Google's free online spreadsheet tool. It works in a web browser and is easy to share.
terms.example: Open the Nkwen Traders sales file in Google Sheets and build a pivot table of sales by branch.

terms.definition: A document that mixes code, its results, charts and text, so you can run and explain an analysis in one place.
terms.example: Your notebook loads the Nkwen Traders sales, calculates totals and explains them in short notes.

terms.definition: Google Colab: a free website that runs Python notebooks in your web browser, with nothing to install.
terms.example: Open the Nkwen Traders starter notebook in Colab and run the first cell.

terms.definition: One box in a notebook that holds code or text. In a spreadsheet, the box where a row and a column meet.
terms.example: Run the cell that loads the Nkwen Traders sales by pressing Shift + Enter.

terms.definition: In Colab, the computer that runs your code. Restarting it clears everything in memory.
terms.example: Choose Runtime > Restart session and run all to check the Nkwen Traders notebook works from top to bottom.

terms.definition: A website that stores your code and notebooks online, keeps the history of every change and lets others see them.
terms.example: You submit the GitHub link to your notebook on Nkwen Traders sales.

terms.definition: A project folder on GitHub that holds your files and the history of all their changes.
terms.example: Your repository has one folder for each chapter, including your Nkwen Traders notebooks.

terms.definition: A saved snapshot of changes to files in a repository, with a short message that says what changed.
terms.example: Make a commit with the message 'Add Mile 4 sales summary' after you upload the notebook.

terms.definition: The front-page file of a repository, usually README.md, that explains what the project is and what is inside.
terms.example: Your README says the project studies Nkwen Traders sales and lists the folders in the repository.

terms.definition: A simple way to format text with symbols, such as # for a heading and ** for bold words.
terms.example: In a text cell, type ## Sales by branch to make a heading above your Nkwen Traders chart.

terms.definition: A popular programming language that is easy to read. Data scientists use it to clean, study and chart data.
terms.example: With Python, you can add up thousands of Nkwen Traders sales in one line of code.

terms.definition: A whole number with no decimal part, such as 0, 25 or -3. In Python its type is int.
terms.example: Store FCFA amounts as integers: price = 35000 for Rice 50kg, not 35000.0.

terms.definition: A number with a decimal point, such as 2.5 or 0.15. In Python its type is float.
terms.example: A 10% discount at Commercial Avenue is stored as a float: discount = 0.10.

terms.definition: Text data written inside quotes, such as "Nkwen". In Python its type is str.
terms.example: branch = "Bafoussam Centre" stores the branch name as a string.

terms.definition: A value that can only be True or False. In Python its type is bool.
terms.example: paid_with_momo = True records that a Nkwen customer paid with Mobile Money.

terms.definition: Python's boolean value for 'yes' or 'correct'. It must start with a capital T.
terms.example: 35000 > 20000 gives True, because a Rice 50kg sale is bigger than 20,000 FCFA.

terms.definition: Python's boolean value for 'no' or 'not correct'. It must start with a capital F.
terms.example: "Mile 4" == "Nkwen" gives False, because the two branch names are different.

terms.definition: Python's value for 'nothing here yet'. It is not zero and not empty text.
terms.example: bill = None means the customer's bill at the Nkwen branch has not been calculated yet.

terms.definition: A Python string that starts with f and puts values inside { }, such as f"Total: {total} FCFA".
terms.example: print(f"{branch} sold {total} FCFA") prints a sentence like 'Mile 4 sold 85000 FCFA'.

terms.definition: A Python collection of values in order, written inside square brackets [ ]. You can change it.
terms.example: daily_sales = [12000, 15500, 9800] is a list of three days of Nkwen branch sales.

terms.definition: The position or label used to find an item. Python lists start at index 0; pandas rows have an index too.
terms.example: In branches = ["Nkwen", "Mile 4"], branches[0] gives "Nkwen", the item at index 0.

terms.definition: Like a list, but written in round brackets ( ), and it cannot be changed after you create it.
terms.example: ("Sugar 1kg", 900) is a tuple that pairs a product with its price in FCFA.

terms.definition: Code that repeats the same steps for each item in a collection, or until a condition stops it.
terms.example: A for loop goes through daily_sales and adds each day's Nkwen sales to the total.

terms.definition: Code that makes a choice: it runs only when a condition is True, using if, elif and else.
terms.example: If a sale is above 50,000 FCFA, label it "large"; else label it "normal".

terms.definition: A Python collection of key-value pairs inside curly brackets { }. You find a value by its key.
terms.example: product = {"name": "Soap", "price": 500}; product["price"] gives 500.

terms.definition: A named block of code you can reuse. It takes inputs, does one job and can return a result.
terms.example: def stock_value(price, qty): return price * qty works for any product at any branch.

terms.definition: A value you give to a function when you call it.
terms.example: In stock_value(35000, 4), the arguments are 35000 (price of Rice 50kg) and 4 (bags in stock).

terms.definition: A name in a function's definition that receives a value when the function is called.
terms.example: In def stock_value(price, qty):, price and qty are parameters.

terms.definition: A function that belongs to a value and is called with a dot, such as name.strip() or df.head().
terms.example: " nkwen ".strip().title() uses two string methods to give "Nkwen".

terms.definition: A short, one-line way to build a new list from another list, often keeping only items that pass a test.
terms.example: [s for s in daily_sales if s > 15000] keeps only the good sales days at Nkwen.

terms.definition: An error that happens while code runs. You can catch it with try and except so the program does not crash.
terms.example: Dividing Mile 4's total sales by zero days raises a ZeroDivisionError exception.

terms.definition: A mistake in code that makes it give a wrong result or stop with an error.
terms.example: A bug counted Nkwen sales twice, so the monthly total looked too high.

terms.definition: Finding and fixing bugs in code, one step at a time.
terms.example: While debugging, print each branch total to see where the Nkwen Traders numbers go wrong.

terms.definition: A Python line that checks something is True. If it is not, the code stops with an error message.
terms.example: assert total > 0, "Total should be positive" checks the Bafoussam Centre sales total.

terms.definition: The Python command that loads a library so you can use its tools.
terms.example: import pandas as pd loads pandas before you read the Nkwen Traders sales file.

terms.definition: A ready-made collection of code that you import and reuse, such as pandas or Matplotlib.
terms.example: Use the Matplotlib library to draw a chart of sales by branch instead of writing chart code yourself.

terms.definition: The spaces at the start of a line. Python uses them to show which lines belong inside a loop, if or function.
terms.example: Lines inside for sale in daily_sales: need indentation of four spaces, or Python gives an error.

terms.definition: The main Python library for tables of data: loading, cleaning, grouping and summarising them.
terms.example: With pandas, you load six months of Nkwen Traders sales and total them by branch.

terms.definition: A Python library for fast maths on arrays of numbers. pandas is built on top of it.
terms.example: np.mean(sales) gives the average daily sale at Mile 4.

terms.definition: A NumPy collection of values that all have the same data type, used for fast maths.
terms.example: sales = np.array([12000, 15500, 9800]) holds three days of Nkwen sales.

terms.definition: A pandas table with named columns and an index for the rows, like a spreadsheet inside Python.
terms.example: df = pd.read_csv("nkwen_traders_sales.csv") loads all the sales into a DataFrame called df.

terms.definition: One column of data in pandas: values in order, each with an index label.
terms.example: df["Branch"] is a Series that holds the branch of every Nkwen Traders sale.

terms.definition: The usual short name programmers give to a pandas DataFrame in their code.
terms.example: df.head() shows the first five Nkwen Traders sales.

terms.definition: Short for data type in pandas or NumPy, for example int64 (whole numbers), float64 (decimals) or object (text).
terms.example: df.dtypes shows Date as object, so convert it with to_datetime before grouping sales by month.

terms.definition: 'Not a Number': the way pandas shows a missing value.
terms.example: A NaN in PaymentMethod means the till did not record how the Mile 4 customer paid.

terms.definition: A list or column of True/False values used to keep only the rows where the value is True.
terms.example: mask = df["Branch"] == "Nkwen"; then df[mask] keeps only the Nkwen branch sales.

terms.definition: The pandas way to choose rows and columns by their labels, or by a True/False condition.
terms.example: df.loc[df["Branch"] == "Mile 4", "TotalSale_FCFA"] gives the amounts of all Mile 4 sales.

terms.definition: A pandas tool that splits rows into groups, calculates something for each group and puts the results together.
terms.example: df.groupby("Branch")["TotalSale_FCFA"].sum() gives total sales for each of the four branches.

terms.definition: To join two tables into one by matching the values in a shared column.
terms.example: Merge the sales table with the branches table on Branch to add each branch's manager to every sale.

terms.definition: A join that keeps every row of the left table and adds matching data from the right table. No match gives a missing value.
terms.example: A left join keeps all sales, even from a branch that is missing in the branches table.

terms.definition: A join that keeps only the rows whose matching value appears in both tables.
terms.example: An inner join drops any sale whose branch is not listed in the branches table.

terms.definition: A join that keeps all rows from both tables and fills the gaps with missing values.
terms.example: An outer join shows branches with no sales and also sales with an unknown branch.

terms.definition: A data type for dates and times, so you can sort them, compare them and take out the month or weekday.
terms.example: After converting Date to datetime, df["Date"].dt.month gives the month of each sale.

terms.definition: A pandas function that turns text like "2026-03-15" into real datetime values.
terms.example: df["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"]) lets you group Nkwen Traders sales by month.

terms.definition: A pandas function (pd.read_csv) that loads a CSV file into a DataFrame.
terms.example: pd.read_csv("nkwen_traders_branches.csv") loads the list of the four branches.

terms.definition: A pandas method that counts how many times each value appears in a column.
terms.example: df["PaymentMethod"].value_counts() shows how many sales were Cash and how many were Mobile Money.

terms.definition: A pandas method that marks each missing value as True. Add .sum() to count them in each column.
terms.example: df.isna().sum() shows how many sales have no PaymentMethod recorded.

terms.definition: A pandas method that fills missing values with a value you choose.
terms.example: df["PaymentMethod"].fillna("Unknown") labels sales with no payment method as Unknown.

terms.definition: The total of all values divided by how many values there are. Also called the average.
terms.example: Sales of 2,000, 3,000 and 7,000 FCFA have a mean of 4,000 FCFA.

terms.definition: The middle value when the values are sorted from smallest to largest. Half are below it, half above.
terms.example: Sales of 2,000, 3,000 and 7,000 FCFA have a median of 3,000 FCFA.

terms.definition: The value that appears most often in the data.
terms.example: If most Nkwen customers buy one bag of rice, the mode of Quantity is 1.

terms.definition: The centre, or typical value, of data. It is usually measured with the mean, median or mode.
terms.example: To describe a typical day at Mile 4, compare the three measures of central tendency.

terms.definition: How far apart the values are. It is measured with the range, IQR, variance or standard deviation.
terms.example: Two branches both average 50,000 FCFA a day, but Bafoussam Centre's daily sales have a much bigger spread.

terms.definition: In statistics, the largest value minus the smallest value.
terms.example: If Nkwen's daily sales go from 30,000 to 90,000 FCFA, the range is 60,000 FCFA.

terms.definition: Roughly the average of the squared distances from the mean. It measures spread; its square root is the standard deviation.
terms.example: Bafoussam Centre has a higher variance in daily sales than Nkwen, so its days are harder to predict.

terms.definition: A measure of spread: roughly the usual distance of values from the mean, in the same unit as the data.
terms.example: A standard deviation of 5,000 FCFA means Nkwen's daily sales are usually about 5,000 FCFA from the mean.

terms.definition: A smaller group taken from a bigger group (the population) and used to learn about it.
terms.example: 200 sales picked from June are a sample of all Nkwen Traders sales.

terms.definition: The whole group you want to know about, not only the part you measured.
terms.example: All Nkwen Traders sales in 2026 are the population; one week of sales is a sample.

terms.definition: How the values of a variable are spread out: which values appear and how often.
terms.example: A histogram shows the distribution of sale amounts: most are small, and a few are very large.

terms.definition: A symmetric, bell-shaped distribution: most values are near the mean, and fewer appear far from it.
terms.example: Daily sales of Palm Oil 5L at Nkwen roughly follow a normal distribution around 40 bottles.

terms.definition: Not symmetric: one side of the distribution has a long tail of very large or very small values.
terms.example: Sale amounts are right-skewed: most are under 10,000 FCFA, but a few wholesale orders are much bigger.

terms.definition: For a normal distribution, about 68%, 95% and 99.7% of values lie within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations of the mean.
terms.example: With a mean of 50,000 and SD of 5,000 FCFA, about 95% of Nkwen's days fall between 40,000 and 60,000 FCFA.

terms.definition: How many standard deviations a value is above or below the mean: (value - mean) / SD.
terms.example: A 65,000 FCFA day at Mile 4, with mean 50,000 and SD 5,000, has a z-score of 3.

terms.definition: A value far away from most of the other values. It may be a mistake or a real but rare event.
terms.example: A 900,000 FCFA sale at Mile 4 is an outlier: check if it is a typing error or a big wholesale order.

terms.definition: Three values that cut sorted data into four equal parts: Q1 (25%), the median (50%) and Q3 (75%).
terms.example: If Q1 is 3,000 FCFA, a quarter of Nkwen sales are 3,000 FCFA or less.

terms.definition: Values that show what percent of the data is below them. For example, 90% of values are below the 90th percentile.
terms.example: The 75th percentile of sale amounts at Commercial Avenue is the amount that 75% of sales are below.

terms.definition: Interquartile range: Q3 minus Q1. It is the spread of the middle half of the data.
terms.example: If Q1 is 3,000 and Q3 is 9,000 FCFA, the IQR of Nkwen sale amounts is 6,000 FCFA.

terms.definition: How likely something is to happen, from 0 (never) to 1 (always).
terms.example: If 300 of 1,000 sales used Mobile Money, the probability that a sale used Mobile Money is 0.3.

terms.definition: The chance that A happens when we already know that B happened. It is written P(A | B).
terms.example: P(Mobile Money | Bafoussam Centre) is the share of Bafoussam Centre sales paid with Mobile Money.

terms.definition: A few numbers that describe data, such as count, mean, median, standard deviation, minimum and maximum.
terms.example: df["TotalSale_FCFA"].describe() gives the summary statistics of all Nkwen Traders sale amounts.

terms.definition: The equal ranges that a histogram puts values into, such as 0-5,000 FCFA and 5,000-10,000 FCFA.
terms.example: With bins of 5,000 FCFA, each bar of the histogram counts the sales in one 5,000 FCFA range.

terms.definition: A number from -1 to 1 that shows how strongly two number variables move together in a straight-line way.
terms.example: Quantity and TotalSale_FCFA have a strong positive correlation: more items means a bigger bill.

terms.definition: When one thing really makes another thing happen. A correlation alone does not prove causation.
terms.example: Umbrella and rice sales at Mile 4 may both rise in July, but one does not cause the other.

terms.definition: A picture of data, such as a bar chart, line chart or histogram.
terms.example: A chart of monthly sales shows the June drop at Bafoussam Centre faster than a table of numbers.

terms.definition: A chart that shows how many values fall into each range (bin). The bars touch each other.
terms.example: A histogram of sale amounts shows that most Nkwen sales are under 10,000 FCFA.

terms.definition: A chart with bars whose length shows a number for each category.
terms.example: A bar chart compares total June sales of the four Nkwen Traders branches.

terms.definition: A chart where points are joined by a line, usually to show change over time.
terms.example: A line chart shows monthly revenue at Commercial Avenue from January to June.

terms.definition: A chart of dots that shows two number variables together, so you can see if they are related.
terms.example: A scatter plot of Quantity against TotalSale_FCFA shows that bigger orders cost more.

terms.definition: A chart that shows the median, quartiles and outliers of data as a box with lines and dots.
terms.example: Box plots of sale amounts for each branch show which branch has the most outliers.

terms.definition: A grid of coloured boxes where the colour shows how big each number is.
terms.example: A heatmap of branch by weekday shows which day is busiest at each Nkwen Traders branch.

terms.definition: One of the lines along the edge of a chart, with a label and units, such as the x-axis or y-axis.
terms.example: Label the y-axis 'Sales (FCFA)' and the x-axis 'Month' on the Nkwen Traders chart.

terms.definition: The key on a chart that explains what each colour, line or symbol means.
terms.example: The legend shows blue for Retail customers and orange for Wholesale customers.

terms.definition: The main Python library for drawing charts.
terms.example: import matplotlib.pyplot as plt lets you plot monthly sales for each Nkwen Traders branch.

terms.definition: The general direction of data over time: going up, going down or staying flat.
terms.example: Mobile Money payments show an upward trend at all four branches from January to June.

terms.definition: Data recorded in time order, such as daily or monthly sales.
terms.example: Monthly revenue at Bafoussam Centre from January to June is a time series.

terms.definition: An organised store of tables that a program can search and update quickly.
terms.example: Nkwen Traders keeps its sales and branches tables in one database.

terms.definition: A question, usually written in SQL, that asks a database for data.
terms.example: A query can return the total Mobile Money sales of each branch for June.

terms.definition: The SQL keyword that chooses which columns to show in the result.
terms.example: SELECT Branch, TotalSale_FCFA FROM sales shows two columns for every sale.

terms.definition: The SQL keyword that names the table to read data from.
terms.example: SELECT * FROM branches reads every column of the branches table.

terms.definition: The SQL keyword that keeps only the rows that meet a condition.
terms.example: WHERE Branch = 'Mile 4' keeps only the Mile 4 sales.

terms.definition: SQL words that make one row per group, so an aggregate like SUM is calculated for each group.
terms.example: SELECT Branch, SUM(TotalSale_FCFA) FROM sales GROUP BY Branch gives one total per branch.

terms.definition: SQL words that sort the result, smallest first by default. Add DESC to put the largest first.
terms.example: ORDER BY total DESC puts the branch with the highest sales at the top.

terms.definition: The SQL keyword that filters groups after GROUP BY, usually with an aggregate like SUM.
terms.example: HAVING SUM(TotalSale_FCFA) > 1000000 keeps only branches that sold more than one million FCFA.

terms.definition: The SQL keyword that combines rows from two tables by matching values in a shared column.
terms.example: sales JOIN branches ON sales.Branch = branches.Branch adds branch details to every sale.

terms.definition: An aggregate that counts rows or values. COUNT(*) counts every row.
terms.example: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sales WHERE Branch = 'Nkwen' gives the number of Nkwen sales.

terms.definition: Adds up all the values in a column, in SQL or in a spreadsheet.
terms.example: SUM(TotalSale_FCFA) gives the total revenue of all Nkwen Traders sales.

terms.definition: In SQL, the marker for a missing or unknown value. It is not the same as zero.
terms.example: A branch with no sales gets NULL for its total after a LEFT JOIN.

terms.definition: Common Table Expression: a named, temporary result made with WITH, then used inside a bigger SQL query.
terms.example: WITH monthly AS (...) first totals sales per month; the main query then compares the months.

terms.definition: A calculation that turns many values into one, such as SUM or COUNT.
terms.example: SUM is the aggregate that turns all of Nkwen's June sales into one total.

terms.definition: A quick check that a result makes sense, such as comparing a total with a number you already know.
terms.example: Sanity check: the four branch totals should add up to the company total for June.

terms.definition: A calculation in a spreadsheet cell. It starts with =, for example =SUM(B2:B100).
terms.example: =SUM(F2:F500) adds up all Nkwen Traders sale amounts in column F.

terms.definition: A summary table that groups rows and calculates totals, for example sales by branch and month.
terms.example: A pivot table shows total sales with branches down the side and months across the top.

terms.definition: A spreadsheet function that finds a value in the first column of a table and returns a value from the same row.
terms.example: =VLOOKUP("Mile 4", A:C, 3, FALSE) finds Mile 4 in column A and returns its value from column C.

terms.definition: A newer spreadsheet lookup that finds a value in one column and returns the matching value from another column.
terms.example: =XLOOKUP("Soap", A:A, C:C) returns the price of Soap, 500 FCFA, if prices are in column C.

terms.definition: Google's free tool for making online reports and dashboards from data such as Google Sheets.
terms.example: In Looker Studio, connect the Nkwen Traders sales sheet and add a bar chart of sales by branch.

terms.definition: Key performance indicator: one of the main numbers a business watches to see if it is reaching its goals.
terms.example: Total monthly revenue per branch is a KPI for Nkwen Traders managers.

terms.definition: A number that you measure or calculate, such as total revenue or number of transactions.
terms.example: In the dashboard, TotalSale_FCFA (Sum) is the metric shown for each branch.

terms.definition: In a report, a category you group or split data by, such as branch, date or payment method.
terms.example: Use Branch as the dimension to show one bar for each Nkwen Traders branch.

terms.definition: To keep only the rows that meet a condition and hide the rest. Also a dashboard control that does this.
terms.example: Filter the sales to show only Mobile Money payments at Commercial Avenue.

terms.definition: A dashboard box that shows one big number, such as total revenue.
terms.example: A scorecard at the top of the dashboard shows total June revenue for all branches in FCFA.

terms.definition: Exploratory data analysis: studying a dataset with summaries and charts to understand it, find problems and see patterns.
terms.example: EDA on Nkwen Traders sales shows weekends are busiest and Mile 4 has many missing payment methods.

terms.definition: About one variable at a time, for example a histogram of sale amounts.
terms.example: Univariate analysis: look at the distribution of TotalSale_FCFA on its own.

terms.definition: About the relationship between two variables, for example sales compared by branch.
terms.example: Bivariate analysis: compare sale amounts between Retail and Wholesale customers.

terms.definition: Data that puts things into groups or labels, such as branch or payment method, not measured numbers.
terms.example: Branch and PaymentMethod are categorical columns in the Nkwen Traders sales data.

terms.definition: Data made of numbers you can calculate with, such as price or quantity.
terms.example: Quantity and TotalSale_FCFA are numeric columns, so you can add them up or take the mean.

terms.definition: What one row of a dataset stands for, for example 'one row = one sale'.
terms.example: The grain of the Nkwen Traders sales table is one row per transaction.

terms.definition: A table that explains each column of a dataset: its name, meaning, data type and example values.
terms.example: The data dictionary says TotalSale_FCFA is a whole number in FCFA: Quantity times UnitPrice_FCFA.

terms.definition: A useful finding from data that helps someone make a decision or take action.
terms.example: Insight: Mobile Money sales at Bafoussam Centre doubled in six months, so add a second payment phone there.

terms.definition: A person who cares about or is affected by your analysis, such as a manager or the owner.
terms.example: The Mile 4 branch manager is a stakeholder in your report on falling rice sales.

terms.definition: A short part at the start of a report that gives the main findings and advice for busy managers.
terms.example: The executive summary says: Mile 4 sales fell 20% in June; restock Rice 50kg before July.

terms.definition: A warning about a limit of your analysis, so readers do not trust it more than they should.
terms.example: Caveat: one week of June data from Bafoussam Centre is missing, so its June total is too low.

terms.definition: Able to be run again by someone else, from top to bottom, giving the same results.
terms.example: Your Nkwen Traders notebook is reproducible if Restart session and run all gives the same totals.
